(B) SOLVED — pointer AND full verbatim primary text retrieved: **SGX Circular No. DT/AM – 50 of 2024, dated 9 September 2024, "Extension of T-session for SGX Japan Derivatives and Intraday Margin Cycle 2 Timing Change"**, issued by Singapore Exchange Derivatives Trading Limited (Co. Reg. 197802854W), signed Leno Lee, Senior Vice President, Trading and Clearing Services, Exchange Platforms. Retrieved as a verbatim 3-page SGX-letterhead PDF mirrored by a member (Fubon Futures) via the Internet Archive; PDF internal CreationDate/ModDate = 2024-09-09.

(A) NOT SOLVED — no circular number found. The only SGX-authored primary documents I could name for the T+1 → 05:15 change are the four Titan DT/DC newsletters (titles + live SGX URLs below), which are the encrypted ones already ruled out. I additionally established the retrieval channel that WOULD hold such a circular verbatim if it had been filed: cftc.gov hosts SGX circulars in full as attachments to SGX-DC's "Weekly Notification of Rule Amendments" (e.g. Circular No. DT/AM – 77 of 2019, dated 8 November 2019, at https://www.cftc.gov/filings/orgrules/rule111219sgx-dcdco002.pdf). I enumerated and downloaded every SGX-DC CFTC filing for 2019 and Jan 2020 (48 PDFs) and read the week-of-14-Oct-2019 and week-of-11-Nov-2019 cover letters: SGX only notifies DC/AM (clearing) circulars there, and no trading-hours circular appears. So the 2019 T+1 circular is NOT in the CFTC mirror.

(B) NO BRACKET NEEDED — the circular states the date itself: effective Monday 4 November 2024 (SGX), one day ahead of JPX/TSE's own 5 November 2024, because 4 Nov 2024 was a Japan public holiday. T session close 2.25 pm → 2.55 pm SGT, exactly the 14:25 → 14:55 move.

(A) TIGHTEST DATED BRACKET THIS CHANNEL SUPPORTS: **2019-10-08 .. 2019-11-11**, both sides SGX-authored artifacts on SGX's own server (dates are HTTP Last-Modified from api2.sgx.com, plus PDF-internal CreationDate where noted).
 - Lower side, 2019-10-08: SGX publishes "Titan DTDC Newsletter - Ext of T+1 Trading Hours Go Live Schedule" (last-modified Tue, 08 Oct 2019 02:12:22 GMT). A "go live schedule" newsletter necessarily precedes go-live.
 - Upper side, 2019-11-11: SGX's own "EN - SGX Mini 10 Year JGB Futures Factsheet - 11 Nov 2019" — filename self-dated 11 Nov 2019, PDF CreationDate Mon 11 Nov 2019, server last-modified Mon, 11 Nov 2019 04:25:47 GMT — states "(T+1) 5:30 pm – 5:15 am".
NARROWING EVIDENCE (consistent with Monday 2019-11-11, but NOT proof): SGX published "Titan DTDC Newsletter - Reminder on Ext of T+1" on Tue, 05 Nov 2019 01:55:31 GMT — a reminder issued the week before, and no further T+1 newsletter after it (the next Titan newsletter, Dec 2019, is "Addition of P Records to SPAN"). If a reminder precedes go-live, the window closes to 2019-11-06 .. 2019-11-11. I flag "reminder precedes go-live" as my inference, not a documented fact.
CAVEAT on one artifact: SGX's "SGX Nifty 50 Factsheet (Eng) - Nov 2019" (PDF CreationDate 2019-11-01, ModDate 2019-11-08, server last-modified Fri, 08 Nov 2019 03:12:48 GMT) already prints "T+1 session: 6.40pm – 5.15am (next day)" three days before 11 Nov. This is forward-looking marketing collateral and must NOT be read as evidence that 05:15 was live on 8 Nov.
INTERMEDIATE 04:45 STEP: I found NO dated artifact of any kind showing 04:45. That side of the sequence is untouched by this channel.
HISTORICAL CONTEXT (outside the bracket, from verbatim SGX press-release mirrors): T+1 close was 01:00 from 11 January 2010 and 02:00 from 30 August 2010.

Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20241114183232/https://www.fubon.com/futures/wcm/home/bulletin/bulletin_20240912_137396/SGXChange.pdf (verbatim SGX-letterhead PDF hosted by member Fubon Futures; live URL now 404)

Header block, verbatim:
"Circular
9 September 2024
Circular No. DT/AM – 50 of 2024
Extension of T-session for SGX Japan Derivatives and Intraday Margin Cycle 2 Timing Change"

Operative sentence, verbatim:
"The Exchange would like to inform market participants that with effect from Monday, 4 November 2024, the T session trading hours for SGX Nikkei derivatives and SGX FTSE Blossom Japan Index Futures will be extended by 30 minutes. This follows the decision of the Tokyo Stock Exchange Inc. (TSE) to extend their trading hours from 5 November 2024, by 30 minutes to 3.30pm Japan Standard Time"

Footnote, verbatim: "4 November 2024 is a Japan public holiday and its underlying cash market is closed."

Section A heading, verbatim: "Effective Monday, 4 November 2024, the contracts for which T session trading hours will be extended by 30 minutes are as follows:" — listing NK, NKO, NR, ND, NU, NS, NC, EJRT, EJP.

Trading-hours table, verbatim (row: NK, NR, ND, NU, NS, NC, EJRT, EJP), Current → Revised (Singapore Time):

dead_ends:
Ruled out in this channel — do not re-run:

1. SGX monthly market-statistics releases, late 2019. The Oct-2019 edition (api2.sgx.com/.../2019-11/SGX Monthly Market Statistics Report Oct 2019.pdf, PDF created 6 Nov 2019) is pure tables — the word "hours" does not occur anywhere in its 32 pages. The Nov-2019 and Dec-2019 editions are NOT at the predictable api2 path (404 on 2019-12/ and 2020-01/ with every naming variant). The Nov-2019 press release (sgx.com/media-centre/20191210-sgx-reports-market-statistics-november-2019, published 10 Dec 2019) was read in full via a mirror: it contains no mention of trading hours, T+1, or any session change. The prose-commentary format that helped on the 2024-08 release did not exist in 2019.

2. SGX investor materials. links.sgx.com/FileOpen/*.ashx returns HTTP 200 with a zero-byte body to non-browser clients; investorrelations.sgx.com/static-files/* returns an Akamai "Access Denied". WebFetch also gets an empty body. FY2020 Annual Report could not be retrieved by any route available here.

3. CFTC. SGX-DT is an FBOT — the CFTC's FBOT filings section holds registration orders only (status values are limited to "Order of Registration Issued / Order Revoking Registration Issued / Pending / Withdrawn"); no rule or trading-hours amendments. SGX-DC (DCO) does file weekly, and those filings DO carry verbatim SGX circulars, but only DC/AM clearing circulars. I enumerated the full SGX-DC filing list for 2019–Jan 2020 from the CFTC filings database and downloaded all 48 attachment PDFs; none mentions T+1, trading hours, or 5.15am. Cover letters for the weeks of 14 Oct 2019 and 11 Nov 2019 were rendered and read (they are scanned images; no OCR binary on this machine, read visually) — the circulars notified in those weeks are margining, member admissions, rubber contract specs and ETPR only.

4. MAS. No public MAS artifact records SGX trading-hours changes; MAS eServices lists SGX-DT as an institution only.

5. SGX rulebook. Futures Trading Rule 4.1.5 explicitly delegates hours out of the rulebook: "The Markets' normal trading hours for each Contract are set forth in the relevant Contract Specifications." So rulebook.sgx.com's dated node-revision history (which does exist, e.g. /node/3063/revisions/9422/view) can never date a session-time change. Regulatory Notice 8.2.1 is SGX-ST cash equities only — it has no derivatives T/T+1 content at all.

6. Vendors, all negative for a dated 2019 bulletin: Databento does not carry SGX at all (SGX is an open feature request on their public roadmap). Trading Technologies' support-updates archive does not reach back to 2019 (earliest SGX T+1 item found is the 27 Nov 2023 US SSF extension; also has the 7 Apr 2025 T+1 revision). Refinitiv/LSEG and ICE Data change notifications are behind customer portals — nothing public. TradingHours.com returns HTTP 403 to WebFetch and publishes no per-market changelog with source citations. Bloomberg, FactSet, Nasdaq Data Link, Polygon, TradingView, Barchart, market-clock.com, QuantConnect, Exegy: current-state hours tables only, no dated change bulletins.

7. Mondovisione is a genuinely verbatim mirror of SGX press releases and is worth keeping in mind, BUT it has no 2019 SGX trading-hours item — only the 2010 pair (extension to 01:00 effective 11 Jan 2010; extension to 02:00 effective 30 Aug 2010). Its www/ article pages also render empty to non-JS clients; the m.mondovisione.com/news/<slug>-<yyyymmdd>/ form is the one that fetches.

8. Broker/member summaries found but NOT usable as a source (member's own words, no circular named): Phillip Nova announcement of 30 Oct 2024; KGI Securities Singapore product pages. KGI does host verbatim SGX circulars at kgieworld.sg/futures/resources/ck/files/docs/ (confirmed: "Circular DTAM 103 of 2020- Launch of SGX FTSE Equity Index Futures.pdf") but the directory is not listable, KGI has no sitemap.xml, and crawling its futures pages surfaced only the 2020 FTSE launch set — nothing from 2019.

9. Wayback CDX for api2.sgx.com is heavily incomplete and the service was intermittently offline during this run (retry on failure — it recovers). Confirmed absent from it: any SGX product factsheet or contract document dated between June 2019 and 8 Nov 2019 that states the T+1 close, i.e. no artifact showing 04:45 was found anywhere. The 04:45 intermediate step remains completely unsourced.

STILL-OPEN LEAD for whoever takes (A) next: the circular exists and is numbered in the DT/AM series. Anchor points established here — DT/AM – 77 of 2019 was issued 8 Nov 2019, and DT/AM – 50 of 2024 was issued 9 Sep 2024 — so a circular issued around the 16 Jul 2019 newsletter would fall roughly in the DT/AM 40s–50s of 2019. The productive route is a member/FCM mirror that keeps dated bulletin folders (the Fubon pattern that cracked (B): www.fubon.com/futures/wcm/home/bulletin/bulletin_YYYYMMDD_NNNNNN/<name>.pdf, dead on the live site but present in the Internet Archive). Taiwanese and Japanese FCMs are the best candidates; Fubon's own bulletin archive has only one SGX item in the Wayback CDX.
